metadata.methods_description: Participants completed separate fMRI and EEG sessions (minimum 2-week interval) while listening to four sections of 'The Little Prince' in Cantonese (~20 minutes total). fMRI acquisition included structural T1-weighted scans, task-based fMRI during listening, and resting-state fMRI. EEG was recorded continuously during listening. Both sessions included comprehension assessments (20 yes/no questions). Cognitive testing (digit span, picture naming, verbal fluency, Flanker task) and questionnaires (Language History Questionnaire 3, Lifetime of Experiences Questionnaire) were administered. MRI data collected at 3T scanner with MRI-safe headphones; EEG recorded with 64-channel cap using foam ear inserts.

citation_details.title: Le Petit Prince Hong Kong (LPPHK): Naturalistic fMRI and EEG data from older Cantonese speakers
citation_details.author: Mohammad Momenian, Zhengwu Ma, Shuyi Wu, Chengcheng Wang, Jonathan Brennan, John Hale, Lars Meyer, Jixing Li
citation_details.abstract: Currently, the field of neurobiology of language is based on data from only a few Indo-European languages. The majority of this data comes from younger adults neglecting other age groups. Here we present a multimodal database which consists of task-based and resting state fMRI, structural MRI, and EEG data while participants over 65 years old listened to sections of the story The Little Prince in Cantonese. We also provide data on participants' language history, lifetime experiences, linguistic and cognitive skills. Audio and text annotations, including time-aligned speech segmentation and prosodic information, as well as word-by-word predictors such as frequency and part-of-speech tagging derived from natural language processing (NLP) tools are included in this database. Both MRI and EEG data diagnostics revealed that the data has good quality. This multimodal database could advance our understanding of spatiotemporal dynamics of language comprehension in the older population and help us study the effects of healthy aging on the relationship between brain and behaviour.
